A new `rt serve` command is registered in `App.cs` with `--solution <path>` and `--port <int>` options (default port 7890)
`rt serve` without `--solution` either errors with exit code 1 or auto-detects a solution per the existing `--solution` auto-detection convention used by other commands
`rt serve` with a non-existent solution path exits with code 1 and prints an error to stderr
`rt serve` with an already-in-use port exits with code 1 and prints a clear error message to stderr
`rt serve` with an invalid port (negative, >65535, non-numeric) exits with code 1 with a clear error
`RoslynTools.Cli.csproj` references `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` framework reference (or the project SDK is changed to `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`) so that ASP.NET Core minimal API types are available
The server is implemented using ASP.NET Core minimal API (no MVC controllers required)
`MsBuildBootstrap.Register()` is invoked before any Roslyn workspace type is loaded in the serve startup path
The MSBuildWorkspace and Solution are loaded exactly once at server startup and registered as singletons in the DI container
The MSBuildWorkspace is disposed when the server stops (Ctrl+C / SIGINT triggers a graceful shutdown)
The server responds to Ctrl+C / SIGINT by shutting down within a reasonable timeout (e.g. <5 seconds) without hanging
`GET /api/capabilities` returns HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: application/json` and a body matching the shape of `rt capabilities --json`
`GET /api/capabilities` JSON includes every command discovered by the reflection-based registry (count matches `App` discovery)
`GET /api/capabilities` JSON includes `OperationParameters` for the 3 adapted commands (describe, find-refs, rename) from US-043
`GET /api/status` returns HTTP 200 with JSON body containing `solution` (absolute path string), `commandCount` (int), and `uptime` (ISO 8601 duration or human-readable string)
`POST /api/execute` with body `{command: "describe", params: {symbol: "..."}, dryRun: false}` returns HTTP 200 with the structured result JSON from `InspectService`
`POST /api/execute` with `dryRun: true` for a mutation command (e.g. rename) returns the diff/preview without writing any files to disk
`POST /api/execute` with an unknown command name returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body containing `error` and `message` fields
`POST /api/execute` with a known command but missing required parameters returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body listing the missing parameters
`POST /api/execute` with malformed JSON body returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
`POST /api/execute` with an invalid parameter type (e.g. integer where string expected) returns HTTP 400 with a JSON error body
`POST /api/execute` for a non-mutating command ignores the `dryRun` flag (or returns 200 normally)
Parameter validation for `POST /api/execute` is driven by the command's `RtCommandInfo.OperationParameters` metadata (not hand-coded per command)
`GET /` returns HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/html` serving the embedded web UI
The web UI HTML and JS are embedded as resources in the `RoslynTools.Cli` assembly (verified by inspecting assembly resources) — they are NOT written to or read from disk at runtime
The web UI loads with no external CDN/script/stylesheet dependencies (works fully offline)
The web UI has no NPM build step — source HTML/JS is committed and served as-is
The web UI on load fetches `GET /api/capabilities` and renders a command browser grouped by `Category` (inspect / analyze / refactor)
The command browser supports text-search filtering across command names and descriptions

Selecting a command in the UI displays a form whose fields are auto-generated from that command's `OperationParameters` (one input per parameter, with type-appropriate widget: text, checkbox, select for enums)
The form marks required parameters visually (e.g. asterisk or required attribute)
The form has a `dryRun` toggle (checkbox) that controls the `dryRun` flag in the POST body
Clicking the `Preview` button calls `POST /api/execute` with `dryRun: true` and renders the response in a `<pre>` element
Clicking the `Apply` button calls `POST /api/execute` with `dryRun: false` and renders the result
The dry-run diff response is rendered with colored added/removed lines using CSS (e.g. green for + lines, red for - lines)
Error responses (400, 404) from `POST /api/execute` are displayed in the UI as a clearly-styled error message (not silently dropped)
An integration test starts the server on an ephemeral port, performs `GET /api/capabilities`, and asserts the JSON contains the expected commands
An integration test performs `POST /api/execute` for `describe` with a valid symbol against a fixture solution and asserts a structured success response
An integration test performs `POST /api/execute` for `rename` with `dryRun: true` and asserts no files on disk are modified after the call
An integration test performs `POST /api/execute` with an unknown command name and asserts HTTP 404 with the expected error body shape
An integration test performs `POST /api/execute` with missing required params and asserts HTTP 400 with the expected error body shape
An integration test performs `GET /` and asserts the response is HTML containing a marker element from the embedded UI
An integration test asserts the server starts and then stops cleanly (host lifetime ends without exception) when the cancellation token is signaled
An integration test asserts the workspace is loaded exactly once across multiple sequential `POST /api/execute` calls (singleton behavior)
`ServeCommand.Info.Category` is a valid category accepted by `App.RunAsync`'s category guard, or the guard is updated to accept `serve` as a top-level mode
`ServeCommand.Info.Mutates` is `false`
`ServeCommand.Info.JsonOutput` is set appropriately
`ServeCommand.Info.Examples` includes at least one realistic invocation (e.g. `rt serve --solution RoslynTools.slnx --port 7890`)
`ServeCommand.Info.WhenToUse` is populated with a clear use-case description
`dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx` passes with no errors or warnings
`dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx -c Release` passes with no errors or warnings
`dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal` passes (all existing tests plus new serve tests)
